# Experiment suppression uses a manifest predicate and a dedicated idempotent blocklist stash

The original suppression feature defaults off. An Experiment is suppressed only when suppression is enabled, its ID is absent from the allowed preference and the install is not temporary. The installed-add-on scan tolerates unavailable resources with allSettled and builds ID:version membership for a dedicated stash. Equal membership returns without a write; changes import that stash with clear:false and await its update. MailGlue rescans on add-on state and suppression-pref changes. The inspected task has no allowed-pref observer. Current status-count filtering adds active/special/allowed flags later. This source does not prove native blocklist effects or release-pref locking.

Scope: Thunderbird Experiment add-on suppression.
